findings.title: SVG contains XML External Entity (XXE) declaration
findings.description: XXE can read local files, perform SSRF, or enable DoS attacks. Attackers use this to exfiltrate environment files or cloud metadata.
findings.attack_path: SVG parsing -> XXE expansion -> file read / SSRF -> data exfiltration
findings.remediation: Remove DOCTYPE and ENTITY declarations. Use a parser with XXE disabled.

findings.title: SVG script uses 'eval(' — arbitrary code execution risk
findings.description: The JavaScript function 'eval(' can evaluate or execute arbitrary strings as code, enabling remote code execution.
findings.attack_path: SVG script -> eval/exec -> arbitrary code execution
findings.remediation: Remove script usage of eval(. Use safer alternatives.

findings.title: SVG inline event handler 'onload' executes JavaScript
findings.description: Event handler 'onload' can fire automatically when the SVG is rendered or parsed. It contains: eval(atob(
findings.attack_path: SVG rendered -> onload fires -> JS executes -> malicious action
findings.remediation: Remove inline event handlers. SVGs should not contain executable content.

findings.title: SVG <script> contains obfuscated JavaScript
findings.description: The script block uses encoding, hex escapes, or other obfuscation techniques to hide its true behavior from code review.
findings.attack_path: SVG rendered/built -> script executes -> contacts C2 -> downloads payload
findings.remediation: Remove the <script> element entirely. SVGs should not contain scripts.

findings.title: SVG script uses 'XMLHttpRequest(' — arbitrary code execution risk
findings.description: The JavaScript function 'XMLHttpRequest(' can evaluate or execute arbitrary strings as code, enabling remote code execution.
findings.attack_path: SVG script -> eval/exec -> arbitrary code execution
findings.remediation: Remove script usage of XMLHttpRequest(. Use safer alternatives.

findings.title: Obfuscated/encoded string found in SVG outside <script> tags
findings.attack_path: Build tooling or parser may process this content unsafely
findings.remediation: Review and remove obfuscated content from SVGs.

findings.title: SVG <foreignObject> contains executable HTML/JS
findings.description: The foreignObject element can embed HTML that executes JavaScript. Attackers use this to bypass SVG-only scanners.
findings.attack_path: SVG rendered -> foreignObject parsed -> embedded script executes
findings.remediation: Remove <foreignObject> elements or sanitize their contents.

findings.title: SVG script makes network request to external URL
findings.description: Script contacts 'https://phishing.example.com/login' — possible C2 callback or payload download.
findings.attack_path: SVG script -> HTTP request -> attacker server -> payload retrieval
findings.remediation: Remove network calls from SVGs. No SVG needs to phone home.

findings.title: SVG contains javascript: URI
findings.description: A link with javascript: URI can execute alert(
findings.attack_path: User clicks SVG element -> javascript: URI executes
findings.remediation: Remove javascript: URIs from SVG files.

findings.title: SVG contains CSS expression or javascript: in style context
findings.description: CSS expressions can execute JavaScript in some renderers.
findings.attack_path: SVG rendered -> CSS expression evaluated -> JS execution
findings.remediation: Remove CSS expressions from SVG styles.

findings.title: Suspicious external URL detected
findings.attack_path: File references https://exfil.example.com/collect -> network request to attacker-controlled server -> data exfiltration / payload download
findings.remediation: Remove or replace the URL. Verify it is necessary and uses a trusted service.

findings.title: Suspicious external URL detected
findings.attack_path: File references https://beacon.example.com/ping -> network request to attacker-controlled server -> data exfiltration / payload download
findings.remediation: Remove or replace the URL. Verify it is necessary and uses a trusted service.

findings.title: Homoglyph attack: 'eval' disguised with Cyrillic characters
findings.description: The identifier 'еval' uses Cyrillic characters that look identical to Latin 'eval' but are different code points. This can hide malicious imports or variable references.
findings.attack_path: Code reviewed as safe -> homoglyph binds to different function -> supply-chain attack
findings.remediation: Replace homoglyph characters with their ASCII equivalents.

findings.title: Network communication — may phone home or download payloads detected

findings.title: Zero-width/invisible Unicode character: U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE
findings.description: Invisible characters can alter code behavior without being visible in editors. Used for obfuscation and hidden control flow.
findings.attack_path: Source appears benign -> invisible chars alter logic -> hidden behavior
findings.remediation: Remove invisible Unicode characters. Use a linter or 'cat -A' to reveal them.
